exposure_fixture.claim: Potential exposure worked out from configuration. No traffic was sent, so this does not show that anything is reachable, and a resource with no finding is not shown to be safe.
exposure_fixture.order: By verdict (potential_exposure, insufficient_data, not_indicated), then rule ID, then resource ID. There is no risk score.

rules.title: Instance open to the internet directly
rules.statement: A running instance with a public address, a security group rule open to the internet, and a route to an internet gateway from its subnet.
assumptions: Network ACLs, host firewalls and anything outside this AWS account are not read.
0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0 are one Internet record, so a rule's address family is not compared with the instance's address.
Whether anything listens on the allowed ports is not read.

rules.title: Instance behind an internet-facing load balancer
rules.statement: A running, healthy target of an internet-facing load balancer whose security group is open to the internet, where the target's security group allows the target port from the balancer.
assumptions: Network ACLs, host firewalls and anything outside this AWS account are not read.
Listeners and their rules are not read, so an open security group is not shown to lead to this target group.
The target group's port is used; a target registered on another port is not seen.
A CIDR rule is not compared with the balancer's addresses, which are not read.

rules.title: Instance one security group rule behind a potentially exposed one
rules.statement: A running instance whose security group allows traffic from the security group of an instance with a potential exposure finding.
assumptions: Network ACLs, host firewalls and anything outside this AWS account are not read.
Only one step is followed; use khonsu explore for longer chains.
Whether the source instance could be made to send this traffic is not assessed.
